title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat)' notes. A class W of weak equivalences in (Cat) is studied in the style of a basic localizer (localisateur fondamental). The previous page proves that W is stable under unions of filtrations by open (or closed) subcategories, provided the induced maps f_i : X_i -> Y_i are in W.

Left half: generalising the index poset to an index category.
(1) Let I be an index category satisfying a hypothesis on the slices I_{/j}. The exact condition is illegible; it is roughly 'non-empty and having the needed infs/filtered'.
(2) Functors phi : X -> I should be identified with filtrations. A filtration here means an increasing map I -> Ouv(X), i -> X_i, from I to the open subcategories (cosieves) of X. It must commute with the relevant colimits and satisfy X = U X_i. He notes that the last condition is equivalent to colim X_i ≅ X.
(3) With this dictionary the comma (fibre) category X_{/i} := X ×_I I_{/i} is exactly X_i. A map f compatible with the filtrations then has f_i : X_i -> Y_i identified with f_{/i} : X_{/i} -> Y_{/i}.
(4) The filtered-union theorem therefore reduces to 'Lemma L3'. This is presumably the localizer axiom / relative Quillen Theorem A: a map over I that induces W-equivalences on all slices X_{/i} -> Y_{/i} is in W.
(5) Corollary: the same holds in a presheaf topos A^. This uses that i_A : A^ -> Cat, F |-> A/F, commutes with arbitrary colimits (it has a right adjoint) and with fibre products. Hence W_A = i_A^{-1}(W) inherits the result.
(6) Tentative corollary ('Cor?'): if the X_i are W-aspherical and I is connected (filtered), then X is W-aspherical. Proof: take Y_i = e, the final category.

Right half: Theorem: the class W is saturated, i.e. f ∈ W iff gamma(f) is invertible in W^{-1}Cat. Corollary: each W_A is saturated (transport along i_A).
Proof sketch:
- Suppose gamma(f) is an iso.
- Using a (homotopical) calculus of fractions, get g : Y -> X' and f' : X' -> Y' with gamma(gf) = gamma(alpha), gamma(f'g) = gamma(beta), where alpha, beta ∈ W.
- After replacing targets (X' -> X'_1, Y' -> Y'_1) and factorising, one may take gf ∈ W and f'g ∈ W.
- One may also take f, g, f' to be open immersions. This is the classical 2-out-of-6 configuration X -> Y -> X' -> Y'.

Next page completes the argument by a telescope:
- Iterating, build a sequence of open immersions X0 -> X1 -> X2 -> ... in which every composite of two consecutive maps lies in W. Set X_inf = colim X_n.
- The map i_0 : X0 -> X_inf is also the colimit of the cofinal subsequence X0 -> X2 -> X4 -> ...
- Each X0 -> X_{2n} is in W. By the filtered-union theorem (open filtrations), i_0 ∈ W; likewise i_1 ∈ W.
- Hence f_0 ∈ W by 2-out-of-3.
In effect this proves the 2-out-of-6 property and saturation from closure under filtered colimits of open immersions, via a mapping-telescope trick.
errors: The step 'par calcul des fractions, il existe g...' presupposes that W admits some (right) calculus of fractions in Cat, at least up to homotopy. W does not admit a strict calculus of fractions in Cat, so this needs justification, e.g. via a homotopy relation '~' and open-immersion replacements. The page only says 'quitte à changer alpha... quitte à factoriser', so this is a gap.
The reduction of f, g, f' to open immersions requires a factorisation of any functor as an open immersion followed by a W-equivalence (mapping-cylinder type). It is invoked but not proved here.

The hypothesis on the index category I (condition on the slices I_{/j}) is not legible and seems not yet settled. The 'Cor?' with its question mark (I connected, X_i W-aspherical implies X W-aspherical) needs I filtered, or at least a condition ensuring the comma categories behave, for the union to be aspherical.

Minor: the claim that 'i_A commutes with arbitrary colimits' is correct because i_A has a right adjoint. The added claim about fibre products also holds (A^/F ≃ (A/F)^). No error here, but it is only asserted.

ideas.what: Filtrations by open subcategories indexed by a category I identified with functors X -> I, with X_i = comma category X_{/i}; filtered-union stability reduced to the slice criterion (Lemma L3).
ideas.modern_name: Stability of basic localizers under filtered colimits (via Grothendieck construction / Quillen Theorem A relative to a base)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks, Les Dérivateurs); systematised by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301) and Cisinski (Astérisque 308)
ideas.where_published: Related material in Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs; exact form unsure

ideas.what: Transfer to presheaf categories via i_A : A^ -> Cat preserving colimits and fibre products; W_A = i_A^{-1} W.
ideas.modern_name: Induced localizer W_A on A^ (test category theory)

ideas.what: Filtered union of W-aspherical open subcategories is W-aspherical.

Saturation of W (and of each W_A): f ∈ W iff gamma(f) is iso. Proved by reducing to a 2-out-of-6 configuration of open immersions, then a telescope X0->X1->X2->... with consecutive composites in W, using cofinality of even terms and filtered-colimit stability.
ideas.modern_name: Strong saturation of basic localizers; 2-out-of-6 via mapping telescope
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006: every basic localizer is strongly saturated, via model structures); 2-out-of-6 formalised by Dwyer–Hirschhorn–Kan–Smith (2004)
ideas.where_published: Saturation questions appear in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs; this telescope proof not known to me in print

missed.claim: A direct, model-category-free proof sketch that W (and W_A) is saturated. It uses only stability under filtered colimits of open immersions plus a telescope trick: in X0->X1->X2->... with consecutive composites in W, the map X0 -> X_inf is the colimit of the W-maps X0 -> X_{2n}. This yields 2-out-of-6 and then saturation. In the literature, strong saturation of basic localizers is obtained by Cisinski through the Thomason-type model structure on Cat.
missed.quote: et $i_0$ est limite des $i_0^{2n} : X_0 \to X_{2n}$, qui sont $\in W$, donc on gagne !!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives an elementary, axiom-level route to (strong) saturation for any class of weak equivalences stable under filtered colimits of 'immersions' with suitable factorisations, e.g. abstract localizers. It also derives 2-out-of-6 from colimit stability alone. It depends on the unproved calculus-of-fractions step, which is the real content to check.

deep.surprise_reason: The results themselves (saturation of basic localizers, filtered-colimit stability) are known through Cisinski and Maltsiniotis. The telescope proof of saturation/2-out-of-6, driven only by filtered unions of open immersions, is a pleasant unpublished argument by Grothendieck. However, its key fractions step is only sketched.
